subject: CedarBridge DPA — SCCs and transfer-impact redlines
messages:
From: Anna Koval <anna.koval@cedarbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Vogel <m.vogel@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: CedarBridge DPA — initial redlines and SCCs matrix

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Our legal team captured a first pass of redlines to the DPA and a separate SCCs crosswalk (attached). High-level asks:

- We have a few carveouts to the standard SCCs around processor subprocessors and export controls (see §3 and §6 inline).
- We need a transfer-impact addendum for non-EEA processing in your hosted region (Germany) that clarifies where logs and telemetry live and whether they are replicated outside the EEA.
- Request a short timeline for whether Redwood can accept our preferred SCCs or propose an equivalent technical safeguard (pseudonymization details are in the matrix).

Attaching: CedarBridge_DPA_initial_marked.docx and SCCs_crosswalk_2028.xlsx.

Can you loop in the internal privacy/legal folks and let us know a target for redline responses? We are targeting contract signature by end of March.

Best,
Anna
Anna Koval

Monica / Ben — can you take the lead on the legal review? Anna — if there are particular clauses you want prioritized beyond the ones called out in your matrix, flag them and we’ll triage.

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: CedarBridge DPA — initial redlines and SCCs matrix

Hi Anna — thanks, I reviewed your markup and the SCCs crosswalk. Below are our proposed positions and open questions.

1) SCCs and processor role language
- Position: we can accept the EU standard SCCs with the usual Redwood-approved processor-to-subprocessor cascade, but we will not accept any broad carveouts that remove our right to appoint subprocessors in the course of delivering service.
- Request: can you confirm which of the carveouts in your spreadsheet are essential versus negotiable? If you can mark the rows "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" that will help speed us up.

2) Transfer-impact addendum (TIA)
- We will prepare a brief TIA that documents: primary processing location (eu-west-1 / Germany), backup replication policy, where logs/telemetry are stored, retention periods, and whether any logs are accessible to support in non-EEA regions.
- Open item: CedarBridge asks for pseudonymization specifics (matrix item 4). We can include high-level descriptions but not specific keys/procedures in contract language; propose an Appendix describing technical measures with references to our security docs.

3) Export controls and law enforcement requests
- Our standard clause provides notification requirements and a narrow challenge process. If you have a specific scenario that concerns you, please share an example so we can address it operationally.

4) Timeline + next steps
- We will produce a consolidated DPA redline + TIA draft by 2028-02-21 for your review. If CedarBridge can return comments within 5 business days, we should be able to finalize before end of March.

Attachments I will produce: a clean TIA draft and a redline showing accepted vs. proposed edits.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Monica Patel

From: Anna Koval <anna.koval@cedarbridge.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Vogel <m.vogel@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 11:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: CedarBridge DPA — initial redlines and SCCs matrix

Thanks Monica — helpful. Quick answers:

- We marked three rows as "must-have" in the SCCs spreadsheet: a) explicit prior notice for any subprocessor outside the EEA; b) a shorter retention cap for diagnostic logs; c) a narrow prohibition on cross-customer data aggregation for analytics (we can provide row numbers).
- The pseudonymization appendix from Redwood sounds acceptable as long as it references the controls and retention you intend to apply.
- For export-control scenarios: our internal security team is mainly asking if Redwood will accept a limited clause that requires notice plus escalation to CedarBridge security for compelled transfer requests. Not asking Redwood to absorb the risk — just cooperation and notice.

We reviewed your note about replication — thanks, that helps. Two other asks:
1) Can your TIA explicitly state whether support access to logs is limited to EEA-based staff unless authorized?
2) Please indicate whether continuity backups are ever stored in the US for disaster recovery, and if so, under what conditions they are restored.

We look forward to the redline + TIA draft.

Best,
Anna

Anna / team — quick operational update and next steps from legal ops:

- Consolidated redline (CedarBridge_DPA_consolidated_redline.docx) is attached. It reflects the positions Monica described and includes two alternative clauses for subprocessor notice (one where we give prior notice and one where we offer a "right to object" window).
- Transfer-impact addendum (attached as transfer-impact-addendum_draft.pdf) documents: primary processing region (eu-west-1), backup replication policy (encrypted backups replicated to eu-west-2; we do not replicate to non-EEA regions except under customer-authorized disaster recovery), and log retention policies (diagnostic logs retained 30 days by default; audit logs 180 days).
- On support access: by default support engineers with access are in the EEA; in exceptional cases we may have US-based on-call staff with emergency access — this will be logged and require pre-authorized escalation and customer notice.

Action items:
1) Anna/Markus: confirm whether the objection-window subprocessor clause is acceptable or if you need the stricter prior-notice-only approach.
2) If CedarBridge needs continuity backups stored in the US for DR, please note the triggering conditions and we can draft a narrow exception with controls.
3) When you are ready we will prepare a DocuSign envelope for the MSA + Order Form + DPA (I’ve included a working DocuSign link below).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Legal Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
